newsitem.title: UK: UK platform orders due after N.Sea fields approved.
newsitem.headline: UK platform orders due after N.Sea fields approved.

text.p: Britain gave formal approval for North Sea oil field development projects on Tuesday and said it expected British fabricators were poised to win major construction contracts as a result.

In a statement, the Department of Trade and Industry said that clearance for Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shearwater project would mean a 300 million stg-plus contract for a constortium led by AMEC Plc for the design, construction, installation and hook-up of its main platform.
Two Scottish yard groups were chasing the 400 million pound main process platform contract for Elf's Elgin/Franklin project.

"Only Scottish yards are left in contention for the main process platform (for Elgin/Franklin). The Barmac yard at Nigg is in competition with a consortium comprising Kvaerner John Brown at Methil and UIE Clydebank for this 400 million pound contract," the DTI statament added.
Elgin and Franklin are being developed for operation by France's Elf and a further 90 million pound wellhead topsides contract is awaited for these fields.
AMEC's Wallsend yard will build the main topsides, bridge and flare boom for Shearwater and Dutch privately-owned Heerema at Hartlepool will share the fabrication work on the contract, the DTI added.

The notification came in the form of a letter of approval to the two operating companies allowing their request to build a pipeline to Bacton, Norfolk, on the English east coast to land gas and oil from the three proposed developments.
